security_audit.summary: Fifty-four of 55 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, relative documentation links, homepage metadata, or ordinary workflow prose. The command on SKILL.md line 52 is a genuine external action because --live sends email through Resend, but dry-run is the documented default. No prompt injection or hidden data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The live seed-send command can transmit campaign content and recipient addresses through Resend.
remediation.suggestion: Keep dry-run as the default, require explicit confirmation immediately before --live, validate all sender and recipient arguments, and quote untrusted shell values safely.

content.user_title: Monitor Inbox Placement and Sender Reputation
content.value_statement: Email teams often lack a clear view of provider placement and sender reputation after campaigns. This skill compares exported telemetry, identifies regressions, and prepares a reusable placement snapshot.
actual_capabilities: Reads seed-list inbox, spam, promotions, and other placement results by mailbox provider.
Summarizes Gmail Postmaster domain reputation, IP reputation, spam rates, and feedback-loop signals.
Summarizes Microsoft SNDS IP status, complaint rates, spam-trap hits, and message volume.
Compares current telemetry with a prior send and names each regression with its magnitude.
Creates a labeled SEND-S placement snapshot and can save it after explicit user approval.
limitations: Requires user-provided seed-test, Gmail Postmaster, Microsoft SNDS, or ESP exports.
Cannot determine placement for providers missing from the supplied seed test.
Does not run SPF, DKIM, or DMARC authentication checks or compute the full email quality score.
Resend automation sends test messages only; users must inspect each seed inbox to classify placement.

use_cases.title: Review a campaign send
use_cases.description: Compare current seed results with the previous campaign and identify provider-specific placement losses.

use_cases.title: Track sender reputation
use_cases.description: Summarize Gmail Postmaster and Microsoft SNDS trends across several sends for an owned domain.

use_cases.title: Prepare a quality-gate input
use_cases.description: Create a labeled placement snapshot for a later email quality assessment and remediation workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize one seed test
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this seed-list result for [domain]. Report inbox, spam, and promotions placement for each provider. Mark every missing provider as NEEDS_INPUT.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one post-send placement test

prompt_templates.title: Compare two sends
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the current and prior placement tests for [domain]. Name every provider regression, show each percentage-point change, and state whether placement is holding.

prompt_templates.title: Trend reputation sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these Gmail Postmaster and Microsoft SNDS exports for [domain]. Report domain and IP direction, complaint changes, spam rates, and trap-hit signals.

prompt_templates.title: Build a complete placement snapshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a SEND-S placement snapshot for [domain] and profile [profile]. Combine seed placement, Postmaster, SNDS, and baseline data without scoring authentication or full EQS.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced handoff for an email quality gate

output_examples.input: Gmail inbox 88%, promotions 12%; Outlook inbox 71%, junk 29%; no Yahoo or Apple results.
output_examples.output: Gmail placement is inbox-dominant. Outlook is degraded because 29% reached junk. Yahoo and Apple are NEEDS_INPUT because no seed results were supplied.

output_examples.input: Current Yahoo inbox placement is 71%; the prior baseline was 96%. Gmail reputation remained High.
output_examples.output: Yahoo regressed by 25 percentage points, from 96% to 71%. Gmail reputation is stable at High. Overall placement is degrading because Yahoo declined.

output_examples.input: Gmail domain reputation changed from High to Medium, and spam rate changed from 0.08% to 0.14%.
output_examples.output: Gmail domain reputation declined from High to Medium. Spam rate increased by 0.06 percentage points and crossed the 0.1% placement threshold.

best_practices: Provide provider-level seed results and exports from the same send window.
Include a prior send baseline so the report can calculate meaningful deltas.
Review recipients and campaign content before approving any live seed send.
anti_patterns: Do not treat missing provider data as a passing placement result.
Do not ask the skill to invent placement percentages from aggregate delivery rates.
Do not use this skill as a replacement for authentication checks or the full email quality gate.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: Provide a sending domain, campaign profile, seed-list placement results, reputation exports, and an optional prior baseline.

faq.question: Which mailbox providers can it compare?
faq.answer: The workflow covers Gmail, Outlook or Microsoft, Yahoo, and Apple or iCloud when those providers appear in the seed test.

faq.question: Does it connect directly to Gmail Postmaster or SNDS?
faq.answer: No. The standard workflow analyzes exports from accounts you control. Optional external tooling may automate related collection or sending.

faq.question: Can it run a seed test?
faq.answer: It documents optional Resend automation for sending seed messages. You must approve live sending and inspect each inbox for actual placement.

faq.question: Does it check SPF, DKIM, and DMARC?
faq.answer: No. Use a dedicated deliverability preflight workflow for authentication checks and static reputation setup.

faq.question: Can it save results for later comparisons?
faq.answer: Yes. After explicit approval, it can save the current snapshot as the baseline for a future send.
